purpose: Independently authored factual spelling grid, fixed before production lookup scoring. It checks a tone-free ASCII input derivative, not full tonal Yale or linguistic approval of dictionary pronunciations.

sources.role: Primary university teaching chart: Yale initials and finals; directly read 2026-10-23 Hong Kong.

Primary university comparison aligning Yale and Jyutping. Indexed table was available; direct retrieval returned an anti-bot page. Cross-check only, with the direct EdUHK and LSHK charts as primary evidence.
Primary explanation of Jyutping j and the jyu versus yyu distinction.
Author's published converter source: supplementary eu-to-ew convention and explanation of low-register h/diacritics. Its kw-to-k differs from the university chart; this grid retains chart-backed kw.

Explicit project input policy requested 2026-10-23: keep marginal final letters a/em/en/ep/et/om/op/um/up/oet while applying ordinary onset conversion. These extra inputs are not claimed to occur in the primary Yale chart.

Pinned published numeric-Yale/Jyutping fields explicitly preserve hm/hng. Reclassified from unverified fallback to supplementary source-backed extension after research; no letters or penalties change and no ordinary-chart or independent linguistic approval is claimed.

policy.tones: Input aliases omit Yale diacritics and the low-register h marker. Numeric Jyutping tones, where the engine supports them, are audited separately without claiming Yale tonal notation.
policy.closed_aa: Only open aa becomes a; closed aai/aau/aam/aan/aang/aap/aat/aak retain aa.
policy.rare: Declared marginal-final extensions have separate project-policy status; other unusual shapes retain canonical Jyutping as an explicitly labelled fallback. Neither class is formal Yale chart coverage.
policy.reuse: Project-authored factual correspondences and examples; no source prose, audio, illustrations or third-party converter code is redistributed.

word_cases.note: Requested casual aa-shortening; not the formal Yale spelling of closed aang.
